title: ICE agents are chasing Miami's Haitians: 'No one goes out anymore, the streets and churches are deserted'
subhead: Since the end, on July 27, of a protective status that had allowed Haitians to reside in the United States, 350,000 of them have faced the threat of deportation by federal immigration authorities. Many no longer dare to leave their homes.

subhead: The student ran an online group specialized in ultraviolence and sextortion. His trial marks the first in France to address 'nihilistic violent extremism,' a movement that originated in the United States.

subhead: Adenot returned to Earth on Thursday after 235 days on the International Space Station, the longest uninterrupted orbital stay by a European astronaut.

title: Swann Arlaud did not want to talk politics
subhead: At 45, Swann Arlaud has remained true to his deeply held left-wing convictions. In May, he risked his career by signing an open letter against the billionaire Vincent Bolloré, who owns French cinema's largest funder. The actor stars as a zealous collaborationist civil servant of the Vichy regime in the newly released 'A Man of His Time.'

subhead: Increasingly criticized after footage emerged showing heavy-handed police tactics and injured teenagers, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez is not toning down his communication. Law enforcement says 6,059 arrests were made between September 28 and October 5, a record number.

title: Trauma endures in Paris suburb after police grenade shatters teenager's jaw
subhead: On September 28, 14-year-old Eden suffered a fractured jaw and lost most of his teeth after he was struck in the face by a tear-gas grenade fired at close range, just a few meters from his high school, where a protest was taking place. Students, teachers and parents spoke of their fear, anger and sense of helplessness.

title: Letter from imprisoned Russian journalist Ivan Safronov: 'Like Jean Valjean, I know what captivity is, and I know how to cherish freedom'
subhead: Safronov, a prisoner of conscience who was arrested in 2020 and is now detained in Siberia, turns to literature as a lifeline. He recently reread Victor Hugo's Les Misérables. Here is the letter he sent to Le Monde about this classic.
